item.title: Nvidia just showed that the harness, not the AI model, is now the real hero
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Nvidia research shows that AI agents can perform well, and not go off the deep end, through fine-tuning, even if the AI model isn't that great at the task.

item.title: The DOJ is investigating a16z. What does this mean for venture capital?
item.dc:creator: Theresa Loconsolo, Anthony Ha, Kirsten Korosec, Sean O'Kane
item.description: Andreessen Horowitz has two partners sitting on the boards of companies that now compete with each other: Ben Horowitz at Databricks and Martin Casado at Fivetran. Nothing too scandalous on the surface, except the Department of Justice has reportedly been investigating the arrangement for almost a year, dusting off a 112-year-old antitrust law that’s rarely used against VCs.  Board conflicts aren’t exactly new, and these companies weren’t necessarily direct competitors when a16z first invested […]

item.title: Starcloud raises $250 million for orbital data centers as launch options dry up
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: There's about to be a big fight to secure access to space.

item.title: AI data startup Micro1 reaches $500M gross run rate amid AI training boom
item.dc:creator: Marina Temkin
item.description: Surging demand for AI training data is driving rapid growth for the startup and its rivals.

item.title: OpenAI is gaining on Anthropic with business users, new data indicates
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Businesses are willing to flop back and forth as each lab releases new models, volatility that should give both companies' investors pause about how "sticky" enterprise AI spending really is.

item.title: ChatGPT can now send texts for you with new Apple Messages plug-in
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: Ever wanted someone else to do your texting for you? ChatGPT is being offered up as an automated text scribe via a new Apple Messages integration.

item.title: OK, can we actually cool data centers with our pee?
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silberling
item.description: Jason Kelce joked that people should cool data centers with their pee, rather than potable water -- but his suggestion is not completely ludicrous.

item.title: Google gives publishers a new way to fight AI-driven traffic losses
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Google is giving publishers a new button that lets readers make them a preferred source across Search, Discover, and Google News, potentially boosting their traffic as AI search sends fewer clicks to the web.

item.title: Runlayer, Rippling drop lawsuits — but the brouhaha is still a cautionary tale for founders
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: Runlayer and Rippling have dropped their lawsuits. No money was paid. Rippling celebrated by releasing a competing product.

item.title: Linkdaze’s smart calendar is built to run a household, not just track a schedule
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: Linkdaze's smart digital calendar stands out for not putting its features behind a paywall, including an AI meal planner tool.

item.title: Grok keeps sending gibberish responses to users
item.dc:creator: Russell Brandom
item.description: Affected users told TechCrunch they were using Grok Lite, and noticed the issues as early as Wednesday morning.

item.title: A third of web pages published since ChatGPT launched were written by AI, study finds
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: ChatGPT and other AI models are now authoring and editing much of the new web.

item.title: Ramp launches its own AI model router, called Router
item.dc:creator: Ram Iyer
item.description: Ramp has launched its own AI model routing service, dubbed Router, that lets users and companies use and switch between various large language models via an API.

item.title: Meta brings Pocket, an app that lets you vibe-code and share games, to US users
item.dc:creator: Sarah Perez
item.description: Meta is bringing Pocket, its experimental AI-powered app for creating and sharing interactive games, to users across the U.S. after quietly testing it in Brazil.

item.title: Inertia Enterprises finds a way to make its fusion fuel fast
item.dc:creator: Tim De Chant
item.description: Fusion power startup Inertia Enterprises reduced the fuel filling process from a week to just a few hours. It's one of 10 hurdles the company must overcome to make a profitable power plant.

item.title: Meta AI’s new Mac app wants you to talk to your apps
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: The company said that the dictation feature works across all apps, just like other tools such as Wispr Flow, Superwhisper, and Monologue.

item.title: Binance now lets AI agents trade, but keeping them in check is largely up to users
item.dc:creator: Jagmeet Singh
item.description: Binance's Agent OS works with tools such as ChatGPT, Claude Code, and Cursor.

item.title: Stripe didn’t really buy OpenRouter because of the ‘singularity’
item.dc:creator: Julie Bort
item.description: What does a payments giant want with a startup that routes prompts between different AI models? Stripe says it's because of "the singularity" but it's really for a far more real and powerful reason.

item.title: OpenAI seeks to one-up Anthropic with new customer privacy protections
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: A competition is developing between OpenAI and Anthropic over who can provide the best privacy protections for enterprise customer data.

item.title: Cognition CEO denies report that SpaceX tried to acquire the startup
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Bellan
item.description: SpaceX was reportedly in talks to buy AI coding startup Cognition. SpaceX has already acquired Cursor as it races to catch up to rivals like OpenAI and Anthropic in enterprise AI.
